summary: Akio Tanabe is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1988, PhD 2006). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (Professor, 2015).

Akira Fujieda (1911–1998) was a sinologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and historian who studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1934). He held posts at Kyoto University from 1937, becoming professor in 1968, and visiting professorships at Copenhagen (1970) and UC Berkeley (1988).
Akira Hataya is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 2014).

Akira Hirakawa (1915–2002) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1962–1975) and taught at Waseda University (1975–1985).

Akira Miyaji is an art historian, Buddhist studies scholar, and Indologist who earned his degrees at Nagoya University. He served as professor at Nagoya University (~1978–2007) and Ryukoku University (2013), and directed the Ryukoku Museum (2013).
Akira Momiyama is a sinology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1981). He served as a professor at Saitama University from ~1996 to 2018.

Akira Mukai is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed his doctoral studies at Hokkaido University (~1971–1976). He served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (~1976–1979) and professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine (1929–2018) studied philosophy, religion, and Buddhism at Kyoto University and Heidelberg University, also studying under Kyoshi Takahama. He served as professor at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (1973), Osaka University (1980–1992), and Ryukoku University (1992).

Akira Sadakata is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Akira Hirakawa, and at the University of Paris. He served as professor at Tokai University from ~1980 to 2006.

Akira Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and earned a PhD from Australian National University. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (2000–2016).

Akira Shimada is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at the College of Art, Delhi, and earned a PhD from SOAS under Daud Ali. He became associate professor at SUNY New Paltz in 2007.

Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1959–1962). He served as an assistant (~1962–1965) and associate professor (1991–1994) at Toyo University.

Akira Takeda (1930–2021) was a sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo from 1961, serving as professor from 1965 to 1991.
Akira Yamada (1922–2008) was a philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi from ~1944 to 1947. He held a post at Nanzan University from ~1953 to 1960.

Akira Yuyama (1932–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who earned a PhD at Australian National University under J.W. de Jong. He directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1976–1995) and taught at Soka University.

Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He served as professor (attested 1982) and professor emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University, and as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

Akong Tulku Rinpoche (1939–2013) was a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre in 1967 and served as its abbot (attested 2009).
Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who pursued doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and is attested as a researcher at Ghent University in 2026.
Akshay Ramanlal Desai (1915–1994) was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at the University of Mumbai from ~1935 to 1946 under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (~1942–1946).

Alain Daniélou (1907–1994) was an Indology, religion, and philosophy scholar who studied at St. John's College and Banaras Hindu University. He served as professor at Banaras Hindu University (1949–1953) and directed research institutes in Pondicherry, Adyar, Berlin, and Venice.
